with $\sigma\in L^{\infty}_+(\Omega)$ for $n=2$ or $\sigma$ Lipschitz continuous for $n=3$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's standing assumptions allow arbitrary n≥2 and merely bounded positive conductivities. The supplied UCP result covers only n=2 and Lipschitz conductivities in n=3. No Lipschitz assumption is imposed on σ_bg in three dimensions, and no UCP result is supplied for higher dimensions. Consequently, the blanket nonexistence assertion does not follow.

failure_location.quote: As a direct consequence of the UCP stated in Theorem~\ref{teo:ucp}, it is not possible to find a non-constant boundary data $g$ fulfilling~\eqref{eqn:idcond}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the nonexistence discussion conditional on the stated UCP hypotheses. Outside that class, leave kernel triviality undecided rather than using it as an established premise.
issues.overall_effect: The repeated claim that the difference operator necessarily has trivial kernel is unsupported over the paper's full conductivity and dimension class.
issues.title: The trivial-kernel conclusion exceeds the supplied UCP hypotheses
issues.why_classification: This requires a substantive qualification of the theoretical scope, but the energy lemma and approximate-kernel procedure do not require universal kernel triviality.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For this particular case, the eigenfucnctions take the form $g_k=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\cos(k\theta)$.

issues.failure_explanation: On the circle of radius R, arclength is R dθ, so the displayed g_k has squared boundary L2 norm R, not 1. The energy-matching equation therefore has right-hand side Rλ_k. The same omission occurs with outer radius r_3 in the hollow example.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the displayed excitation and use Rλ_k in the disk energy equation, giving the estimator R*(k*σ_bg*λ_k/R)^(1/(2k)); make the analogous r_3 correction in the hollow example.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-k radius formulas are incorrectly scaled for general outer radius. The R=1 plot and the stated limiting radii are unaffected.
issues.title: The circular radius estimators omit the boundary normalization factor
issues.why_classification: Tracking the boundary measure supplies a routine local correction without changing the method, examples at unit radius, or asymptotic conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Indeed, the fundamental requirement to reconstruct an anomaly $A$ is the possibility to find a proper excitation on $\partial\Omega$ able to produce an electric current density flowing in all the domain $\Omega$ but not in the region $A$.

issues.failure_explanation: The monotone radial power density explains why this sublevel-set method fills the hole; it does not establish physical non-identifiability. The displayed boundary eigenvalues retain nontrivial dependence on r_1. For fixed conductivities and r_2, changing the inner radius changes these data, with the signal tending to zero as the shell thickness tends to zero. Producing an exactly excluded current field is not established as a necessary condition for inversion from the full NtD map.

failure_location.quote: The impossibility to correct reconstruct hollow anomalies derives from an intrinsic limit of the physical problem considered.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the impossibility claim to reconstruction by the proposed single-field power-density sublevel sets, rather than asserting intrinsic loss of the hole information in boundary measurements.
issues.overall_effect: A limitation of the chosen reconstruction criterion is presented as a limitation of the underlying inverse problem.
issues.title: The hollow-anomaly obstruction is incorrectly attributed to the inverse problem
issues.why_classification: The source supports a comparable algorithmic obstruction, but the broader physical impossibility claim must be withdrawn.

issues.failure_explanation: Boundedness of N supplies neither self-adjointness nor a discrete spectrum for Λ_n. On a double eigenspace from the circular example, a norm-δ skew-symmetric perturbation produces eigenvalues λ±iδ, which cannot be ordered decreasingly as asserted. A noncompact bounded perturbation can also destroy the assumed discrete eigenvalue enumeration. The stated hypotheses therefore do not support the kth-eigenvalue bound.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Formulate and use the bound for self-adjoint finite-dimensional compressions, with symmetrized measurements and consistently paired boundary coordinates. Do not extend that ordered-eigenvalue conclusion to arbitrary bounded operator noise without additional spectral hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The general noisy-operator eigenvalue comparison and the spectral procedures premised on an ordered real spectrum are not justified.
issues.title: Bounded noise does not justify the ordered-eigenvalue perturbation theorem
issues.why_classification: A standard self-adjoint matrix formulation retains the intended norm-error estimate and numerical setting, but the unrestricted operator theorem requires substantive replacement.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing E_D=∫_D σ_bg|∇u_bg|² and Q=P-P_b, the upper monotonicity estimate gives Q≤[(σ_bg^M-σ_a^m)/σ_a^m]E_D, not Q≤(Δ_σ/σ_a^m)E_D. For example, take σ_bg=2, u_bg=x_1, and σ_a equal to 1 and 1.9 on equal-volume halves of D. Then E_D=2|D| and the preceding valid inequality gives Q≥0.55|D|, whereas the claimed lower bound requires E_D≥10Q≥5.5|D|.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lower coefficient by σ_a^m/(σ_bg^M-σ_a^m), and update subsequent uses of that endpoint.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound and the parameter interval derived from it are false for the admitted spatially varying conductivities.
issues.title: The lower energy bound uses the minimum contrast where an upper contrast is needed
issues.why_classification: The correct coefficient follows by a routine extremal estimate and preserves a two-sided energy comparison over the same conductivity class.

issues.failure_explanation: The preceding estimates constrain total power in D, not the pointwise density cutoff ε. The two threshold prescriptions are already incompatible in the paper's homogeneous disk example: for R=1, σ_bg=2, σ_a=1, r_i=1/2 and k=2, the formulas give λ=1/94 and p=r²/(2π). The final energy-matching rule gives ε=1/(π√94), so ε/λ=√94/π>2, outside the asserted interval 1<α<2. This defect persists when the extrema bound is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Distinguish an integrated power budget B from the density level ε. Apply the corrected energy inequalities only to B, and determine ε through the cumulative-energy equation ∫_{p<ε}p=B, with appropriate feasibility and tie handling.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed analytical admissibility interval for the density threshold is unsupported, and the preliminary and final threshold constructions disagree.
issues.title: Integrated power bounds are incorrectly turned into density-threshold bounds
issues.why_classification: The threshold construction and its claimed justification must be recalibrated, but the source already supplies a comparable energy-budget approach.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The plateau of the eigenvalues around the noise level causes an abrupt change in the slope of the curve, depicted in Figure~\ref{fig:eign}, which makes easy to identify the reliable eigenvalues.

issues.failure_explanation: An upper perturbation bound does not imply a noise floor or a plateau. Let K be the positive noiseless difference and let N=δP_1, where P_1 projects onto its first eigenfunction. This is bounded, compact and self-adjoint: only the first eigenvalue shifts, while every tail eigenvalue remains unchanged and tends to zero. Thus the prescribed 'last eigenvalue before the plateau' need not exist even after repairing the perturbation theorem's hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Identify the last eigenvalue $\overline{\lambda_k}$ of $\Lambda_n$ before the plateau and the corresponding eigenfunction $\overline{g_k}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a supplied noise-norm bound to define an explicit spectral cutoff, rather than requiring a visible plateau, and specify an insufficient-data branch when no mode passes the cutoff.
issues.overall_effect: The final algorithm lacks a defined eigenfunction-selection step for admissible noise, and its automatic detection of reliable modes is not guaranteed.
issues.title: The eigenfunction-selection step assumes a noise plateau that need not exist
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement of the selection rule is necessary; the same spectral method can remain, but the asserted universal plateau behavior cannot.

issues.failure_explanation: The admitted regime σ_a>σ_bg makes Λ_σD−Λ_σbg negative semidefinite. In the circular examples its nonzero eigenvalues are strictly negative. Even without noise, the proposed output equation then equates a nonnegative integral to a negative number, so no reconstructed set exists. The same untreated sign makes the analytic radius radicands negative.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Orient the difference operator according to the contrast: use Λ_σD−Λ_σbg for less-conductive anomalies and its negative for more-conductive anomalies. Order the resulting nonnegative spectrum and use its positive quadratic form, with the corresponding monotonicity constants, throughout.
issues.overall_effect: The stated reconstruction procedure does not operate on the advertised more-conductive-anomaly regime.
issues.title: The reconstruction energy equation is impossible for more-conductive anomalies
issues.why_classification: A routine sign-aware case distinction repairs the construction without excluding either contrast regime or changing the method.

The electric potential is discretized with a piece-wise linear function, as the boundary potential, while the imposed normal component of current density $g$ is discretized by a piece-wise constant function on the boundary elements.

issues.failure_explanation: No condition ensures that the target lies in the attainable energy range. In the analytic disk family with R=1, σ_bg=3, σ_a=1, r_i=0.9 and k=1, the formulas give λ=54/119, while the total background power is only 1/3; no subset can satisfy the equation. Independently, F(ε)=∫_{p<ε}p can have jumps: p is constant for the k=1 disk mode and is elementwise constant in the stated uniform-background, piecewise-linear FEM implementation. Increasing ε therefore need not ever attain an exact prescribed budget.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Check the budget against the total background power before accepting a mode, and provide a failure branch if no feasible mode exists. Replace exact threshold attainment by a generalized-quantile rule, with a stated tolerance or explicit treatment of positive-measure level sets.
issues.overall_effect: The output region and the threshold-search termination are not guaranteed, even for positive contrast signals and the paper's own discretization.
issues.title: Exact sublevel-energy matching is not guaranteed to be attainable
issues.why_classification: The procedure needs feasibility checks and a revised threshold/tie construction; these are contained changes, but exact matching cannot simply be presumed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: while the boundary $\partial\Omega$ is given by $N_b=256$ elements of the same length.

The electric potential is discretized with a piece-wise linear function, as the boundary potential, while the imposed normal component of current density $g$ is discretized by a piece-wise constant function on the boundary elements.

issues.failure_explanation: Elementwise current coefficients and nodal voltage coefficients use different boundary spaces and duality pairings. For equal edge length h, the nodal load is b_j=h(g_{j-1}+g_j)/2. Thus the raw voltage matrix has the form SB, not the symmetric energy matrix B^T S B, and need not have a real ordered spectrum. Moreover, because N_b is even, the nonzero mean-zero alternating flux g_j=(-1)^j satisfies Bg=0 and produces zero FEM potential for every conductivity. This supplies an anomaly-independent spurious kernel mode.

failure_location.quote: In this discrete setting, the NtD operator is a linear map from the $N_b$ values of $g$ on the boundary elements to the $N_b$ values of the boundary potential on the boundary nodes.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a common resolved boundary space for currents and voltages, with its L2 mass matrix, and form the corresponding self-adjoint Galerkin eigenproblem. For example, use nodal piecewise-linear functions for both quantities; otherwise explicitly remove fluxes annihilated by the load map.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical eigenproblem does not automatically inherit continuous self-adjointness or the intended near-kernel interpretation, and can select unresolved flux modes rather than anomaly information.
issues.title: The discrete current-to-nodal-voltage matrix lacks the spectral structure being used
issues.why_classification: A compatible discrete operator and eigenproblem must be constructed and the numerical calculations checked again, but this is a contained discretization repair.

issues.failure_explanation: Symmetrizing the full Gaussian matrix does not make it preserve the zero-mean boundary subspace. With equal-length boundary elements, compatibility requires Σ_j g_j=0, whereas a generic stated noise realization mixes this subspace with the constant vector. The eigenvectors of the resulting full noisy matrix therefore need not be admissible Neumann data, so applying them directly can make the subsequent direct problem unsolvable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compress the data and noise to the mean-zero space before diagonalization. For equal boundary lengths, use Π=I−11^T/N_b, replace N by ΠNΠ, and solve the eigenproblem only on the range of Π.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical noise model and eigenfunction-to-direct-solve step do not enforce the current conservation required by the continuous problem.
issues.title: The synthetic noise construction does not preserve Neumann compatibility
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local compatibility projection; it preserves symmetry and does not increase the noise norm or change the intended reconstruction regime.
